title: Background work without freezing the window
when: Importing, indexing or exporting in the desktop app freezes the window or shows not responding, and the work needs progress and cancel.
inputs: the heavy job and its input size
prompt:
Goal: Heavy jobs run off the UI thread with progress, cancel and errors reported, so the window keeps repainting.
Steps:
1. Move CPU work into worker.js: const w = new Worker("js/worker.js", { type: "module" }); post the input, receive { type: "progress" | "done" | "error" } messages.
2. Keep workers pure: no DOM, no native calls; the main thread reads files and passes text or ArrayBuffers (transfer them with postMessage(buf, [buf])).
3. Post progress at most every 100 ms with done and total counts; the UI shows a <progress> and an estimate.
4. Cancel: a button calls w.terminate() and resets state; for soft cancel post { type: "cancel" } checked between chunks.
5. When a worker is not possible, chunk the loop: process 500 items, then await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0)) before the next batch.
6. Long file writes: queue them and await each Neutralino.filesystem call; never block with busy loops.
7. External tools, if truly needed, run with Neutralino.os.spawnProcess and fixed arguments, never a shell string built from user input.
8. worker.onerror and message errors show a readable message and re-enable the buttons.
Quality bar:
- The window stays responsive during a 100 MB import.
- Cancel stops within one second.
Pitfalls:
- Posting progress for every item, which floods the UI.
- Copying huge buffers instead of transferring them.
Verify:
- [ ] Heavy loops live in the worker or yield.
- [ ] Cancel and error paths reset the UI.
- [ ] No shell strings with user input.
Output: worker.js, jobs.js and the progress markup.

examples.input: quando importo arquivo grande o app desktop congela
examples.output: Module worker with progress every 100 ms, transferable buffers, terminate on cancel, chunked fallback
